title: Go bag
tldr: Pack a portable bag with the essentials you need to leave quickly: medicines, documents, contact information, water, food, light, phone power and weather-appropriate clothing. Keep it light enough to carry and a separate grab list for items used every day.
steps: Know where you can go and how you will get there.
Include medication arrangements, identification copies, keys and accessible supplies.
Pack water, snacks, light, charger, hygiene supplies and appropriate clothing.
Carry the bag briefly, reduce excess weight and refresh dated items.
next: Keep bags accessible and plan for pets, infants and mobility equipment.
watch: Never delay an urgent evacuation to finish packing.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: If you have minutes rather than days, grab essential medicines, documents, shoes, water and a phone charger first. Divide necessary supplies among people who can carry them, without giving children or a person with limited mobility an unmanageable load.
household: Pack for actual infants, pets, access needs and the likely transport mode. Agree which adult carries shared items and who stays with each dependent. Include a destination plan; a bag does not establish that a shelter will admit or support the household.
pack_now: Prioritize supplies named in this guide that are usable by the person who needs them. Keep the checklist and relevant contact details accessible. Check carrying capacity, storage and equipment instructions in advance; collecting equipment must not delay the immediate protective action.
faqs: Does a stocked bag make leaving easier?

Only if it can be reached and carried while managing dependents. Test the load and remove duplication. Keep essential medicine, documents and mobility aids accessible; do not bury a critical item beneath optional equipment.
What if I cannot take the bag?

Leave when immediate danger requires it. Reaching safety takes priority over retrieving supplies. Keep a short written contact plan with each person and identify an alternate source of essential support ahead of time where possible.
scope: Civilian educational guidance. Linked references may use U.S. emergency systems; local warning methods, laws, services and conditions differ.
